DEMO-BMF-01.title: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing: issuing obligation and transition rules

summary.title_en: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing: issuing obligation and transition rules
summary.summary: From 1 January 2027, businesses with prior-year turnover above EUR 800,000 must issue structured e-invoices (XRechnung or ZUGFeRD from version 2.0.1, excluding the MINIMUM and BASIC-WL profiles) for taxable domestic B2B supplies under § 14 UStG. For these businesses PDF and paper invoices are no longer permitted after the transition period. Recipients may lose input VAT deduction on invoices that do not meet the structured format.
summary.who_is_affected: Businesses with prior-year turnover above EUR 800,000 that make taxable domestic B2B supplies, and their B2B customers who may lose input VAT deduction on non-compliant invoices.

Recipient relies on input VAT deduction on an invoice that does not meet the structured format
exclusions: Structured invoices in the MINIMUM and BASIC-WL profiles do not meet the format requirement

summary.summary: The publication reports a BFH ruling that the continuation-loss rule of § 8d KStG does not apply where a company added a new line of business or significantly changed its customer segment during the observation period, so loss carryforwards were forfeited under § 8c KStG in the case at hand (a software company expanding from small-business to enterprise customers after a financing round). DEMO-BFH-03.title: Extended trade tax reduction: photovoltaic systems on let properties

summary.title_en: Extended trade tax reduction: photovoltaic systems on let properties
summary.summary: The BFH held that income from rooftop photovoltaic systems and tenant electricity on let properties is harmful to the extended trade tax reduction under § 9 No. 1 sentence 2 GewStG once it exceeds 10% of rental income in a given year, and that planned expansions must be assessed year by year. Property companies are advised to review PV expansion plans and consider moving PV systems into a separate entity.

memo.headline: From 1 January 2027 Müller must issue structured e-invoices (XRechnung or ZUGFeRD) for domestic B2B supplies, but its Sage 100 (2019) system only produces PDFs and the ERP migration has no approved budget.
memo.impact: With prior-year revenue of EUR 48.2m (FY2023), Müller is far above the EUR 800,000 threshold, so the obligation applies from 1 January 2027 to its taxable domestic B2B supplies. After the transition period, PDF and paper invoices are no longer permitted for these supplies, and the update does not state how long that period lasts. Sage 100 (on-premise, version 2019) supports neither XRechnung nor ZUGFeRD, and the ERP migration is planned only 'in 2026 or later' with no budget approved. Customers, including automotive suppliers (approx. 60% of sales) and medical device manufacturers (approx. 40%), may lose input VAT deduction on invoices that do not meet the structured format, which could put those relationships under strain. The export share of approx. 55% does not remove the need to act, because cross-border supplies are only 'not yet covered' and the domestic B2B volume remains in scope.
memo.deadline: 1 January 2027 (transition period for PDF and paper invoices applies, duration not stated)
recommended_actions: Decide now whether to bring forward and fund the ERP migration or to upgrade or supplement Sage 100 so it can issue XRechnung or ZUGFeRD (version 2.0.1 or later, excluding the MINIMUM and BASIC-WL profiles).
Map which invoices are domestic taxable B2B supplies (in scope) and which are cross-border, VAT-exempt or to private individuals (not covered), so the scope of the system change is clear.
Check with key customers in the automotive and medical device sectors which structured format they can receive, so that their input VAT deduction is not put at risk.
Include the e-invoicing readiness assessment, already an open point in the due diligence report, in a dated project plan with a named owner and budget request.
memo.proposed_mandate: E-invoicing readiness review and implementation support: scope analysis of domestic B2B invoice flows, format and system requirements for Sage 100 or its successor, and a timeline and budget case for the managing directors.
questions_for_client: How long is the transition period for PDF and paper invoices? The update does not state it and it must be confirmed from the official source.
What share of invoices and revenue relates to taxable domestic B2B supplies versus cross-border or exempt supplies?
Is there a current status or decision date for the ERP migration, and can a budget be approved before 1 January 2027?
Can Sage 100 be extended with an add-on or external tool to produce XRechnung or ZUGFeRD as an interim solution?
Which formats do the main customers require or accept, and do any already send structured e-invoices to Müller?
Does the invoicing of chain transactions via the Polish subsidiary involve any domestic B2B invoices that fall under the new rules?

memo.headline: The BFH ruling undercuts Brightloop's planned fallback on § 8d KStG, putting the approx. EUR 21m loss carryforwards (approx. EUR 6.3m future tax benefit) at real risk of forfeiture ahead of the Series B closing.
memo.impact: Brightloop's shareholder base has changed by more than 50% across Seed (2020), Series A (2022) and Series B (2024), so the approx. EUR 21m of loss carryforwards is already exposed under § 8c KStG, and management intends to rely on the continuation-loss rule (§ 8d KStG) as protection. The BFH ruling, as reported, says that rule does not apply where a company added a new line of business or significantly changed its customer segment during the observation period, and the taxpayer must prove an unchanged business operation with detailed documentation. Brightloop shows both warning signs: a new route-optimisation product line in 2023 and a shift from small logistics firms to enterprise customers (42 enterprise customers, up from 6 in 2022), which mirrors the software company in the ruling. Its documentation of business continuity is also incomplete, so the burden of proof would be hard to meet. If the loss carryforwards were forfeited, the indicative future tax benefit of approx. EUR 6.3m would be lost, which matters for the Series B tax due diligence (report date 2 October 2024, closing 12 November 2024).
memo.deadline: none stated (the update does not give an effective date; internal timeline: due diligence report 2 October 2024, Series B closing 12 November 2024)
recommended_actions: Build the defence file for the loss carryforwards now, documenting what the business operation looked like before and after each financing round, including products, customer base and Stripe Billing records.
Re-assess whether reliance on § 8d KStG is still tenable given the 2023 product line and the move to enterprise customers, and set out the risk and options openly in the due diligence report.
Clarify the observation period under § 8d KStG and the effective date of the ruling, and test how both apply to the Seed, Series A and Series B share transfers.
Discuss with management how the possible loss of the approx. EUR 6.3m tax benefit should be reflected in the financing discussions with Northwind Ventures Fund IV LP and in tax planning.
memo.proposed_mandate: Loss carryforward protection review: assess § 8c/§ 8d KStG exposure in light of the BFH ruling, build the business-continuity defence file, and support the Series B due diligence disclosure.
questions_for_client: What exactly is the observation period for § 8d KStG, and when did it start and end relative to the Seed, Series A and Series B share transfers?
Is the ruling effective for past periods or only going forward? The update does not state an effective date.

Can management document that the business operation was unchanged despite the 2023 route-optimisation product line and the move from small logistics firms to enterprise customers (310 customers, 42 of them enterprise)?
What business-continuity documentation already exists, and what is missing?
Have any loss carryforward positions already been assessed or confirmed by the tax authority, and is any § 8d KStG application already filed?

memo.headline: The BFH ruling puts Nordlicht's extended trade tax reduction at risk once the planned PV roll-out on six more buildings from 2025 pushes PV income above 10% of rental income in any single year.
memo.impact: The BFH held that income from rooftop PV and tenant electricity on let properties is harmful to the extended trade tax reduction under § 9 No. 1 sentence 2 GewStG once it exceeds 10% of rental income in a given year, and that planned expansions must be assessed year by year. Today Nordlicht is well within the limit: 2022 feed-in income from the two existing PV systems was EUR 41k against rental income of EUR 11,400k. The planned PV systems on six further buildings from 2025 would bring approx. EUR 1.3m income per year once complete, which is a very different order of magnitude and must be tested against the 10% threshold for each year. Exceeding the threshold in one year removes the extended reduction for that entire year, not just for the excess, so the stakes are the reduction on the whole rental income. The ruling also suggests that moving PV systems into a separate entity is an option, but whether that fits Nordlicht, especially in light of Project Polarstern, has not yet been assessed.
recommended_actions: Model the 10% test year by year for 2025 onwards, using projected rental income and the phased PV income from the six further buildings (approx. EUR 1.3m per year once complete), including any tenant electricity income.
Review and, if needed, re-sequence the PV roll-out plan before commitments are made, so that the timing does not push PV income above 10% of rental income in any year.
Assess moving the existing and planned PV systems into a separate entity, as the ruling suggests, and check the consequences for the current structure and the Polarstern ownership set-up.

Include the ruling in the ongoing review of the PV expansion plan against the extended trade tax reduction, together with the open review of operating equipment (Betriebsvorrichtungen) in the two commercial units.
memo.proposed_mandate: Advisory engagement to model the 10% threshold for the PV expansion plan year by year and to evaluate options, including a separate PV entity, to protect the extended trade tax reduction.
questions_for_client: What is the projected rental income for 2025 and later years, so that the 10% threshold can be tested for each year?
How will the PV roll-out on the six further buildings be phased and timed, and when will each system start generating income?
Does Nordlicht also earn tenant electricity income in addition to feed-in income, and if so, how much?
Has moving the PV systems into a separate entity already been considered, and are there any constraints from the Project Polarstern structure or the financing?
Are the approx. EUR 1.3m of annual PV income figures a full-year estimate once all six systems are complete, and do they include any tenant electricity income?

memo.headline: The BMF's updated guidance supports a Forschungszulage claim for Müller Präzisionstechnik's titanium implant process work, with an indicative potential of EUR 1.1m–1.6m, and the earliest years may be time-limited, so the claim should be evaluated now.
memo.impact: Müller Präzisionstechnik has never filed a research allowance claim, although its internal R&D team of 14 FTE develops new machining processes for medical-grade titanium implants with technical uncertainty. The BMF confirms that internal process innovations such as new manufacturing methods qualify as experimental development if they involve technical uncertainty, and that claims for eligible expenses from 2020 onwards can still be filed within the four-year assessment period. R&D expenses of EUR 1.6m were recognised in FY2023 (of which EUR 1.3m personnel costs), and the due diligence report indicates a potential of EUR 1.1m–1.6m for FY2020–FY2023. A BSFZ certificate is required for each R&D project and the client has none; because BSFZ processing times have increased, applications for older projects should be submitted promptly. The opportunity is not guaranteed: it depends on the projects qualifying and on whether the assessment period for the earliest years (FY2020, FY2021) has already expired.
memo.deadline: none stated as a fixed date; claims for eligible expenses from 2020 onwards must be filed within the four-year assessment period, and applications for older projects should be submitted promptly (guidance published 2026-10-13)
recommended_actions: Confirm for each year FY2020–FY2023 whether the four-year assessment period is still open, starting with FY2020 and FY2021, to determine which years can still be claimed.

Identify and document the individual R&D projects (new machining processes for medical-grade titanium implants) and the technical uncertainty in each, so BSFZ certificate applications can be prepared.
Submit BSFZ certificate applications promptly, prioritising older projects, given the increased processing times.
Quantify eligible expenses (including personnel costs) for FY2020–FY2023 to refine the indicative EUR 1.1m–1.6m potential before filing claims.
memo.proposed_mandate: Forschungszulage readiness and claim mandate: project scoping, BSFZ certificate applications and preparation of research allowance claims for FY2020–FY2023.
questions_for_client: For which of the years FY2020–FY2023 is the assessment period still open, and has any assessment already become final?
What were the R&D expenses and the potentially eligible amounts (especially personnel costs) in FY2020, FY2021 and FY2022, in addition to the EUR 1.6m in FY2023?
Which individual R&D projects exist, when did each start, and how is the technical uncertainty documented for each?
Was any BSFZ application ever started or any external funding received for these projects?
Given the fiscal unity with Müller Holding GmbH, who would be the claimant and how should the claim be coordinated at the tax group level?

memo.headline: The BMF's revised transfer pricing rules put the 5% cost-plus remuneration and outdated 2019 documentation of Müller Precyzja squarely in focus just as a tax audit for FY2021–FY2023 is expected in 2026.
memo.impact: The BMF letter says that tax auditors may request the transaction matrix within 30 days of an audit order, that benchmarking studies for routine contract manufacturers must not be older than three years, and that cost-plus markups of 5% or less will be reviewed with particular scrutiny. Müller Precyzja Sp. z o.o. is paid cost plus 5% under the agreement of 1 July 2019, based on a 2019 benchmarking study, and the Local File covering FY2019–FY2021 has not been updated. With EUR 7.4m of purchases from the Polish subsidiary, and an audit for FY2021–FY2023 expected in 2026, the client meets several of the letter's trigger points at once. Missing or outdated documentation can lead to estimates and surcharges of up to EUR 1m, and the due diligence report already put the indicative markup-adjustment exposure at EUR 0.4m–0.9m. In addition, the agreement requires a markup review every three years, but none has been documented, which weakens the client's position. The letter does not address related-party financing, so that topic is not affected by this update.
memo.deadline: No effective date stated in the update; the 30-day transaction matrix deadline runs from the date of an audit order, and the client's audit for FY2021–FY2023 is expected in 2026.
recommended_actions: Commission a new benchmarking study for the Polish contract manufacturing arrangement to replace the 2019 study, and test whether the 5% markup is still arm's length.
Update the Local File beyond FY2021 (FY2022 and FY2023 at minimum) and document the missing three-year markup review required by the 1 July 2019 agreement.
Prepare the transaction matrix now so it can be delivered within 30 days of an audit order, and set up an internal process and responsible persons for this.

Assess the exposure under different markup scenarios against the EUR 0.4m–0.9m indicative range from the due diligence report and the up to EUR 1m estimate/surcharge risk, and decide whether any adjustment to the agreement is advisable.
memo.proposed_mandate: Transfer pricing documentation package: new benchmarking study, updated Local File for FY2022–FY2023, transaction matrix preparation and audit-readiness support for Müller Precyzja.
questions_for_client: Has an audit order for FY2021–FY2023 already been issued or announced by the tax office?
From when do the revised administrative principles apply, and do they cover the open years FY2021–FY2023? The update states no effective date.
Has any markup review under the 1 July 2019 agreement been carried out informally, even if not documented?
Is a transaction matrix or any other transfer pricing documentation available for FY2022 and FY2023?
Does Müller Precyzja carry out only routine manufacturing for the Company, with the Company bearing market and inventory risk, as described in the due diligence report?

memo.headline: The BMF's updated research allowance guidance puts Brightloop's approx. EUR 0.6m 2023 claim (AI-based scheduling engine) at concrete risk until the missing BSFZ application is filed, so it should not wait until after the 12 November 2024 closing.
memo.impact: The BMF says a BSFZ certificate is required for each R&D project and that applications for older projects should be submitted promptly because processing times have increased. Brightloop has a certificate for the 2022 project only; the 2023 AI-based scheduling engine has none, although a claim of approx. EUR 0.6m was already filed for it. The update does not state a threshold, fee or separate effective date, and it covers eligible expenses from 2020 onwards within the four-year assessment period. Whether further claims for 2020 or 2021 exist, or whether internal process innovations could add eligible projects, cannot be told from the profile.
memo.deadline: No separate effective date or deadline is stated; the guidance was published 2026-10-13 and covers eligible expenses from 2020 onwards within the four-year assessment period. The BSFZ application for 2023 is currently planned after the 12 November 2024 closing, and the update says to submit promptly.
recommended_actions: Bring forward the BSFZ application for the 2023 AI-based scheduling engine project instead of waiting until after closing, and confirm who prepares it and when it can be filed.
Reflect the approx. EUR 0.6m 2023 claim and the pending BSFZ status accurately in the Series B tax due diligence disclosure as an open point with a clear timetable.

Check whether any internal process innovations with technical uncertainty exist that could qualify as experimental development.
memo.proposed_mandate: Research allowance review and BSFZ application support: secure the 2023 claim of approx. EUR 0.6m, screen open years from 2020 onwards, and align the disclosure in the Series B due diligence.
questions_for_client: When exactly is the BSFZ application for the 2023 project planned to be submitted, and has any preparatory work started?

DEMO-BFH-02,DEMO-BMF-01.subject: Brightloop Software GmbH: B2B e-invoicing and loss carryforwards
DEMO-BFH-02,DEMO-BMF-01.body:
We advised Brightloop on the tax due diligence for the Series B financing in 2024. I am writing about two recent developments.

1. Mandatory B2B e-invoicing: From 1 January 2027, Brightloop would need to issue structured e-invoices for its German B2B subscriptions. Your Stripe Billing PDF invoices may no longer be permitted once the transition period ends. As German customers generate 45% of your revenue, recipients may lose input VAT deduction, which may cause friction with your enterprise customers.

2. Loss carryforwards: Your shareholder base changed by more than 50% across three financing rounds, so your loss carryforwards of approx. EUR 21m are exposed under § 8c KStG. A recent BFH ruling reads the continuation-loss rule in § 8d KStG strictly and may deny it after a new line of business or a significant change in customer segment. Brightloop launched a route-optimisation product in 2023 and moved towards enterprise customers, which appears similar to the case decided. The tax benefit of approx. EUR 6.3m may be at risk.

This assessment is based on the information from our 2024 review, and your position may have changed since.

I suggest a 30-minute call within the next two weeks to review your Stripe Billing set-up, the German invoices and your § 8c/§ 8d KStG exposure and business-continuity documentation.

Please suggest a time, or reply with any questions.

DEMO-BFH-03.subject: Nordlicht Immobilien: PV expansion and extended trade tax reduction
DEMO-BFH-03.body:
In 2023 we supported Nordlicht Immobilien GmbH & Co. KG with the tax due diligence for Project Polarstern. I am writing about a recent BFH ruling that may affect your planned photovoltaic roll-out.

The ruling concerns the extended trade tax reduction (§ 9 No. 1 sentence 2 GewStG). It holds that income from rooftop photovoltaic systems and tenant electricity is harmful once it exceeds 10% of rental income in a given year. Planned expansions are assessed year by year. Nordlicht is well within the limit today: 2022 feed-in income from your two systems was EUR 41k against rental income of EUR 11,400k. The planned systems on six further buildings from 2025 would bring approx. EUR 1.3m per year once complete. Exceeding the threshold in one year is likely to remove the reduction for that entire year, so it may affect your whole rental income. The ruling also mentions a separate PV entity. We have not yet assessed whether that fits Nordlicht in light of Project Polarstern.

This assessment is based on the information from our 2023 review, and your position may have changed since.

I suggest a 30-minute call within the next two weeks. We would model the 10% test year by year from 2025, review the sequencing of the roll-out and assess a separate PV entity.

Please let me know a time that suits you, or reply with any questions.
